713642.t: Contracted from φάος (pháos). After the contraction, the original s-stem was changed into a t-stem φωτ- (phōt-), following ἔρως (érōs), stem ἐρωτ- (erōt-) and χρώς (khrṓs), stem χρωτ- (khrōt-).

713686.t: Unknown, perhaps Pre-Greek. Probably cognate, ancestor, or descendant of Latin calx (“limestone, chalk”).

713640.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰōnā́, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰoh₂-néh₂, from *bʰeh₂- (“to speak”) (whence φημί (phēmí, “to say, speak”)).

713633.t: Inherited from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH-tís. By surface analysis, φύω (phŭ́ō, “grow”) + -σις (-sĭs).

713665.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰəřřō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰer-. The iota in the progressive forms (present system) is a reflex of the *y marker for the present tense added onto the root χαρ- (khar-).

713609.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰugā́, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰugéh₂. Equivalent to φεύγω (pheúgō, “flee”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

713620.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH-lom, from *bʰuH- (“to be, grow”). By surface analysis, an old derivative from φῦναι (phûnai), active infinitive of an aorist form ἔφυν (éphūn) of φύω (phŭ́ō, “to bring forth”).

713667.t: Likely from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰelh₂d- (“hail; hoarfrost”). Cognate with Proto-Slavic *žȇldъ (“glazed frost, sleet”), Persian ژاله (žâle, “hail”).

713622.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰol-yom, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₃- (“leaf, blossom, flower”). Cognates include Latin folium, Old Armenian բողբոջ (bołboǰ), and English blossom.

713623.t: A variant of φυλή (phūlḗ, “tribe”), itself related to φύω (phúō, “to beget”).

713695.t: Unknown. Has been compared to Proto-Slavic *želězo (“iron”), Latin ferrum, and Hittite [script needed] (ḫapalki-).

713638.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰúyō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuHyéti, from *bʰuH- (“to appear, become, rise up”).

713637.t: From φυτός (phŭtós, “natural; which has grown naturally”), from φύω (phúō, “to generate; cause to grow”).

713619.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰulát͏̌t͏̌ō, equal to φύλαξ (phŭ́lăx, “watcher, guard”) + *-ϳω (*-jō). Further etymology is unknown.

713662.t: Related to χάσκω (kháskō, “to open the mouth, gape, yawn”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂-n- of the same meaning.

713616.t: Same source as φυλάσσω (phŭlắssō, “to guard; to watch”), but of unknown further etymology. According to Beekes, both words are clear examples of Pre-Greek.

713685.t: According to Beekes, a Pre-Greek origin is probable, as it is difficult to explain "χαλ-" from Indo-European and as a suffix "-ιν-" is frequent in Pre-Greek.

713611.t: Borrowed from a Semitic language, such as Hebrew פּוּךְ (pūk, “eye-rouge, antimony”).

713674.t: According to Beekes, of unknown or Pre-Greek origin, and unrelated to Armenian խաղ (xaġ, “game, pastime”) (a connection would require a Proto-Indo-European *kʰ, which is unheard of for inherited words).

713603.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰerǵ- ~ *bʰreǵ- (“to roast, fry”), though the phonetics are irregular, suggesting a loanword from a third unidentified party.

713601.t: From φρύγω (phrū́gō, “to roast”) + -ανον (-anon), as dry firewood was traditionally used to start fires and roast food.

713675.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew חֶלְבְּנָה (ḥɛlbənɔ̂), from the root ח־ל־ב (ḥ-l-b) related to milk, from Proto-Semitic *ḥalīb- (“milk; fat”).

713632.t: From φυσάω (phūsáō, “to blow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, agent noun suffix).

713610.t: From φύω (phúō, “to grow, to be . . . by nature”) + -η (-ē, nominal suffix).

713630.t: Uncertain, with Beekes suggesting Pre-Greek origin based on the opaque phonology and semantic domain. May be related to φορύνω (phorū́nō, “to be mingled”) and/or πορφύρω (porphū́rō, “to heave, surge up”).
